description: The image displays a series of five bar charts, each illustrating a distinct distribution pattern of parameter allocation across layers in a neural network, as part of the “Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Design Spaces” paper. From left to right, the first chart, unlabeled but visually showing a strictly increasing trend, depicts a distribution where parameter allocation grows progressively from left to right, with bar heights approximately proportional to 1, 2, 3, and 4 units. The second chart, labeled “Uniform,” shows four bars of equal height, indicating an even distribution of parameters across all layers. The third, labeled “Decreasing,” presents a descending pattern with bar heights roughly 4, 3, 2, and 1, reflecting a reduction in parameter allocation from early to later layers. The fourth, labeled “Spindle,” shows a symmetric distribution with low values at the ends and higher values in the middle — approximately 1, 3, 3, and 1 — resembling a spindle shape. The fifth, labeled “Bottleneck,” displays a U-shaped pattern with higher allocation at the first and last layers and lower in the middle — approximately 3, 1, 1, and 3 — mimicking a bottleneck structure. All bars are rendered in a uniform light green color with black outlines, and each chart is positioned above its corresponding label on a horizontal axis with no numerical scale, emphasizing relative proportions rather than absolute values. The overall layout is clean and schematic, designed to visually contrast different parameter allocation strategies.
